title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Seizure, Impoundment, and Freezing of Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts

articles.content_en:
Article 1 When a People's Court seals up, distrains, or freezes the chattels, immovables, or other property rights of a person subject to enforcement, it shall make a ruling and serve it on the person subject to enforcement and the person applying for enforcement.
If the adoption of sealing up, distraining, or freezing measures requires the assistance of a relevant entity or individual, the People's Court shall prepare a notice of assistance in enforcement and serve it together with a copy of the ruling on the person assisting in enforcement. The ruling on sealing up, distraining, or freezing and the notice of assistance in enforcement shall take legal effect upon service.

Article 2 A People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze the chattels in the possession of the person subject to enforcement, the immovables, specific chattels, and other property rights registered in the name of the person subject to enforcement.
For unregistered buildings and land-use rights, the ownership shall be determined based on the approval documents for the land-use right and other relevant evidence.
With respect to chattels in the possession of a third party or immovables, specific chattels, and other property rights registered in the name of a third party, if the third party confirms in writing that such property belongs to the person subject to enforcement, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze them.

Article 3 After the legal instrument serving as the basis for enforcement takes effect and before an application for enforcement is filed, the creditor may apply to the People's Court with enforcement jurisdiction for the preservation of the debtor's property. The People's Court may, by reference to Article 92 of the Civil Procedure Law, make a preservation ruling, which shall be executed immediately.

Article 4 If property preservation measures are taken before litigation, during litigation, or during arbitration, after the enforcement procedure commences, they shall automatically be converted into sealing up, distraining, or freezing measures during enforcement, and the provisions of Article 29 of these Provisions on the time limits for sealing up, distraining, or freezing shall apply.

Article 6 A People's Court may seal up a residential house that is necessary for the daily life of the person subject to enforcement and his/her dependents, but shall not auction, sell, or use it to satisfy the debt.

Article 7 With respect to houses and daily necessities that exceed what is necessary for the daily life of the person subject to enforcement and his/her dependents, the People's Court may, upon the application of the person applying for enforcement and after ensuring the residential house and ordinary daily necessities necessary for the minimum subsistence standard of the person subject to enforcement and his/her dependents, proceed with enforcement.

Article 8 When sealing up or distraining chattels, the People's Court may directly take control of such property. If the People's Court delivers the sealed up or distrained chattels to another person for control, it shall affix seals to such chattels or adopt other appropriate methods sufficient to publicize the sealing up or distraining.

Article 9 When sealing up immovables, the People's Court shall post seals or a public notice, and may take and retain the relevant title documents.
When sealing up, distraining, or freezing registered immovables, specific chattels, or other property rights, the People's Court shall notify the relevant registration authority to go through the registration formalities. If the registration formalities are not completed, such actions shall not prevail against other sealing up, distraining, or freezing actions for which registration formalities have been completed.

Article 10 When sealing up a building for which ownership registration has not yet been carried out, the People's Court shall notify its manager or the actual possessor of the building, and post a public notice in a conspicuous place.

Article 11 When distraining a motor vehicle for which ownership registration has not yet been carried out, the People's Court shall record the engine number of the motor vehicle on the distraint list. If during the period of distraint, the right holder requests to go through the ownership registration formalities, the People's Court shall permit it and promptly handle the corresponding distraint registration formalities.

Article 12 If the sealed up or distrained property is not suitable for custody by the People's Court, the People's Court may designate the person subject to enforcement to be responsible for its custody; if it is not suitable for custody by the person subject to enforcement, it may entrust a third party or the person applying for enforcement with its custody.
If the property is designated by the People's Court to be in the custody of the person subject to enforcement, and continued use will not materially affect the value of the property, the person subject to enforcement may be permitted to continue using it; if the property is in the custody of the People's Court or is entrusted to a third party or the person applying for enforcement, the custodian shall not use it.

Article 13 When sealing up, distraining, or freezing secured property in the possession of a security interest holder, the security interest holder shall generally be designated as the custodian; if such property is in the custody of the People's Court, the pledge or lien shall not be extinguished by the transfer of possession.

Article 14 With respect to property co-owned by the person subject to enforcement and other persons, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze it and shall promptly notify the co-owners.
If the co-owners agree to partition the co-owned property by agreement and the creditor approves, the People's Court may deem such partition effective. The effect of the sealing up, distraining, or freezing shall extend to the property within the share of the person subject to enforcement after the partition; the sealing up, distraining, or freezing of property within the shares of other co-owners shall be released by the People's Court by a ruling.
If a co-owner initiates a partition action or the person applying for enforcement initiates a subrogated partition action, the People's Court shall permit it. During the pendency of the action, enforcement of the property shall be suspended.

Article 15 With respect to the property of the person subject to enforcement that is in the possession of a third party for the benefit of the person subject to enforcement, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze it; if such property is designated for continued custody by the third party, the third party shall not deliver it to the person subject to enforcement.
With respect to the property of the person subject to enforcement that is lawfully in the possession of a third party for the third party's own benefit, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze it, and the third party may continue to possess and use such property, but shall not deliver it to the person subject to enforcement.
If a third party has borrowed the property of the person subject to enforcement without compensation, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not apply.

Article 16 If the person subject to enforcement sells his/her property to a third party, the third party has paid part of the price and actually possesses the property, but the person subject to enforcement retains ownership under the contract, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze the property; if the third party requests continued performance of the contract, the third party shall pay the full balance to the People's Court within a reasonable period, and the People's Court shall rule to release the sealing up, distraining, or freezing.

Article 17 If the person subject to enforcement sells property that requires registration of transfer to a third party, the third party has paid part or all of the price and actually possesses the property, but the registration of the transfer of title has not yet been completed, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze the property; if the third party has paid the full price and actually possesses the property, but the registration of transfer has not been completed, and the third party is not at fault in this regard, the People's Court shall not seal up, distrain, or freeze the property.

Article 18 If the person subject to enforcement purchases property from a third party, has paid part of the price and actually possesses the property, but the third party retains ownership under the contract, and the person applying for enforcement has paid the remaining price to the third party or the third party has agreed in writing that the remaining price shall be satisfied preferentially from the proceeds of the sale of the property, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze the property.
If the third party dissolves the contract according to law, the People's Court shall permit it, and the sealing up, distraining, or freezing measures that have been taken shall be released; however, the People's Court may, upon the application of the person applying for enforcement, enforce the creditor's right of the person subject to enforcement against the third party arising from the payment of the price.

Article 19 If the person subject to enforcement purchases from a third party property that requires registration of transfer, has paid part or all of the price and actually possesses the property, and although the registration of the transfer of title has not been completed, the person applying for enforcement has paid the remaining price to the third party or the third party has agreed that the remaining price shall be satisfied preferentially from the proceeds of the sale of the property, the People's Court may seal up, distrain, or freeze the property.

Article 21 The sealing up, distraining, or freezing of the property of the person subject to enforcement shall be limited to an amount sufficient to satisfy the creditor's rights determined in the legal instrument and the enforcement costs, and shall not clearly exceed the subject matter amount.
If it is discovered that the sealing up, distraining, or freezing exceeds the subject matter amount, the People's Court shall, upon the application of the person subject to enforcement or ex officio, promptly release the sealing up, distraining, or freezing of the portion of the property exceeding the subject matter amount, unless the property is indivisible and the person subject to enforcement has no other property available for enforcement or other property is insufficient to satisfy the debt.
Article 22 The effect of sealing up or distraining shall extend to the accessories and natural fruits of the sealed up or distrained property.

Article 23 The effect of sealing up a building above ground shall extend to the land-use right within the scope of use of the building, and the effect of sealing up a land-use right shall extend to the building above ground, unless the ownership of the land-use right and the building above ground belong separately to the person subject to enforcement and another person.
If the registration authorities for the building above ground and the land-use right are not the same authority, the sealing up registration shall be handled separately.

Article 24 If the sealed up, distrained, or frozen property is lost or damaged, the effect of the sealing up, distraining, or freezing shall extend to the substitute property or compensation money of the property. The People's Court shall promptly make a ruling to seal up, distrain, or freeze such substitute property or compensation money.

Article 25 If, at the time a notice of assistance in enforcement for sealing up, distraining, or freezing is served on the registration authority, the registration authority has already accepted an application for registration of transfer of immovables, specific chattels, or other property by the person subject to enforcement but has not yet approved the registration, the registration authority shall assist the People's Court in enforcement. The People's Court shall not take measures of sealing up, distraining, or freezing against the property that the registration authority has already approved the transfer of by the person subject to enforcement.
If, at the time a notice of assistance in enforcement for sealing up, distraining, or freezing is served on the registration authority, another People's Court has already served a notice of assistance in enforcement for transfer registration on the same registration authority, the transfer registration shall be processed with priority.

Article 26 Any transfer, creation of an encumbrance, or other act that impedes enforcement by the person subject to enforcement with respect to property that has been sealed up, distrained, or frozen shall not be asserted against the person applying for enforcement.
If a third party, without permission from the People's Court, takes possession of the sealed up, distrained, or frozen property or engages in other acts that impede enforcement, the People's Court may, upon the application of the person applying for enforcement or ex officio, remove such possession or eliminate such obstruction.
If the People's Court's sealing up, distraining, or freezing has not been publicized, its effect shall not be asserted against a bona fide third party.

Article 27 When the People's Court seals up or distrains a mortgaged property on which the person subject to enforcement has created a maximum amount mortgage, it shall notify the mortgagee. The amount of the debt secured by the mortgage shall no longer increase from the time the mortgagee receives the notice from the People's Court.
Even if the People's Court has not notified the mortgagee, if there is evidence proving that the mortgagee knew of the fact of the sealing up or distraining, the amount of the debt secured by the mortgage shall no longer increase from the time the mortgagee learned of such fact.

Article 28 With respect to property that has already been sealed up, distrained, or frozen by a People's Court, other People's Courts may make subsequent sealed up, distraining, or freezing (waiting list). When the sealing up, distraining, or freezing is released, the waiting list sealing up, distraining, or freezing that was registered first shall automatically take effect.
If another People's Court makes a waiting list sealing up, distraining, or freezing of registered property, it shall notify the relevant registration authority to assist in making the waiting list registration, and the People's Court that carried out the sealing up, distraining, or freezing shall allow the other People's Court to inspect the relevant documents and records.
If another People's Court makes a waiting list sealing up, distraining, or freezing of unregistered property, it shall make a record, which shall be signed by the enforcement personnel of the People's Court that carried out the sealing up, distraining, or freezing and the person subject to enforcement, or it shall notify the People's Court that carried out the sealing up, distraining, or freezing in writing.

Article 29 The period for a People's Court to freeze the bank deposits and other funds of the person subject to enforcement shall not exceed six months; the period for sealing up or distraining chattels shall not exceed one year; the period for sealing up immovables or freezing other property rights shall not exceed two years, unless otherwise provided by laws or judicial interpretations.
If the person applying for enforcement applies for an extension of the period, the People's Court shall, before the expiration of the period of sealing up, distraining, or freezing, go through the procedures for extending the sealing up, distraining, or freezing; the extended period shall not exceed one-half of the period specified in the preceding paragraph.

Article 30 If the period for sealing up, distraining, or freezing expires and the People's Court has not gone through the extension procedures, the effect of the sealing up, distraining, or freezing shall be extinguished.
If the sealed up, distrained, or frozen property has been auctioned, sold, or used to satisfy the debt through enforcement, the effect of the sealing up, distraining, or freezing shall be extinguished.
Article 32 These Provisions shall apply to the enforcement of rulings on property preservation and advance execution.

Article 33 These Provisions shall come into force as of January 1, 2005. If any judicial interpretation previously promulgated by this Court before these Provisions come into force is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
